A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPROUT framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation evaluations, reproduced baseline comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds pretrained-model comparisons, stain-perturbation experiments, runtime comparisons, and component ablations.

M1.justification: The stain-derived self-reference, prototype construction, POT-Scan, activation prompting, and containment-aware NMS procedures remain unchanged. Newly tested decoder, clustering, and sampling alternatives are ablations rather than revisions to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: MoNuSeg, CPM17, TNBC, PanNuke, and the qualitative DSB2018 fluorescence demonstration already appear in v1. v2 adds controlled stain/color perturbation scenarios in Appendix D.3. Whole-slide deployment is discussed but not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds Cellpose, CellViT, CellSAM, and PathoSAM as evaluated pretrained comparators, substantially strengthening the comparison set beyond the retained Table 1 baselines. Table 7 also introduces direct runtime comparisons against U-Net, MedSAM, and COIN.

E3.justification: Original dataset splits, resizing procedures, and segmentation metrics are retained. Added experiments introduce Macenko/Vahadane normalization, specified color and optical-density perturbations, and a SAM-b-based comparison of domain-adapted decoders. These extend the evaluation protocol without establishing changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive tests of stain robustness, SAM versus domain-adapted decoders, K-means versus K-means++ and GMM, and foreground/background prompt-sampling strategies (Tables 6, 19, 20, and 22). These address additional questions about dependence on stain cues and component choices beyond v1's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times and average performance is reported. Neither adds seed values, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The new perturbation magnitudes are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained, but substantial new results are added. For example, v2 Table 4 reports CellViT AJI of 0.657/0.703 versus SPROUT's unchanged 0.621/0.662 on MoNuSeg/CPM17. New robustness, latency, and component results broaden the findings. The new Table 3 also inconsistently assigns TNBC/PanNuke PQ, DQ, and SQ values relative to the detailed tables.

T1.justification: The method equations, Appendix A transport derivations, equivalence proof, solver algorithms, and Appendix B.2 metric definitions are retained. Pagination and typesetting differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the central training-free, annotation-free prompting contribution and broad performance claims. Naming PanNuke in the introduction corrects the description of coverage already present in v1 rather than establishing a new contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D explicitly interprets the gap to pretrained models and the tradeoff between higher inference latency and avoiding training. New Appendix G.2 discusses deployment and identifies failures from corrupted stain cues, misleading backgrounds, and biased prototypes propagated through POT-Scan. Added ablations also receive substantive mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: New Table 2 consolidates implementation settings and identifies UNI2 and three nearest negative prompts as general defaults; sensitivity experiments still specify Virchow2 and two negatives. Appendix F.1 adds valid-grid-cell sampling details. These are documentation additions, not evidence that the original settings changed. Hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the new pathology and SAM comparators, along with additional citations in the introduction and related work. Appendix D.1 positions pretrained pathology models as upper-bound references, while Section 4.1 calls the original baselines representative. The central training-free novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized wording edits, an equal-contribution note, corrected dataset-count wording, a separate quantitative-study appendix, and a practical Q&A. Existing runtime and ablation material is reorganized without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially with configuration and performance summaries plus dedicated baseline, perturbation, runtime, decoder, clustering, and sampling comparisons. Existing figures are retained but several are enlarged or relocated; UMAP and runtime displays exchange numbering. Figure 24(c)'s label is corrected from negative to positive points.

improvement.justification: The stronger comparisons, stain-robustness tests, component ablations, and explicit latency and failure discussions make v2 better supported and more useful. However, new Table 3 introduces metric-column inconsistencies for TNBC and PanNuke, and the conclusion retains broad superiority language despite the stronger models reported in Table 4. These reporting weaknesses temper the gains, yielding a qualified overall improvement.
